waiting.result: Polar of an Aequus (proved): the polar about the centre, in a sphere of any radius, has curvature 4π/N at every corner (Theorem 1, normalisation stated). The polar is fair exactly when the die has equal curvature at every corner (Theorem 2). Exhaustive over the 15 192 catalogued Aequi: exactly 24 have a fair polar (Aequus CO-14, CORD-26, DI-32, D·I·RT-62 and 20 dihedral dice; equality exact by orbit, by Gram congruence, or by an exact π/3 identity). For the other 15 168 the polar is proved not fair (certified-distinct curvatures). The polars of Nos. 1233–1235 (the permutahedra) are not fair

waiting.result: Stellation cycle under polarity (proved): in a sphere of radius² φ^m, I_k↔D_{m−2−k}, SSD(k)↔GD(m−3−k), GSD(k)↔GI(m−5−k); closed exactly when the radius² is a power of φ; the Vacuus (15 mirrors) is kept and the Resonus is exchanged with the corner planes. Midsphere reciprocals: SSD(k)→GD(k−1) (corners ×φ⁻¹), GSD(k)→GI(k−1). Scope: refuted outside the regular members (five cubes: 30 Vacuus planes, none a mirror ↔ five octahedra: 15 mirrors)

waiting.result: Faceting ladder (proved): with corners fixed, the regular facetings of I_k and D_k are SSD(k−1), GD(k−1), GI(k−3), GSD(k−3), so the dual ladder is the stellation cycle read downwards, not a second cycle. Every faceting of the icosahedron keeps its Vacuus in the 15 mirrors and its Resonus in 16 of the 31 hub planes. Facetings of the dodecahedron using cube edges or cube face diagonals leave the mirrors
waiting.goes_to: the Vacuus and Resonus paper; stellation-cycle write-up

waiting.result: Sphere inversion about the centre (proved): central planes are fixed, so the Vacuus, Resonus and Sphericus great circles are unchanged. Faces go to spheres on the diameters from the centre to the polar's corners, tangent at the centre to the Resonus planes. Edges go to circles in the Vacuus plates. The inverted body is the pedal body of the polar. It is never convex, so constant width is proved impossible (convex polyhedra and every star-shaped polyhedral body, interior centre). Exact Sphericus table of edge circles for the five Platonic polyhedra and the four Kepler–Poinsot stars
